diagnostic_evidence.quote: Then there exists a constant $\zeta > 0$ such that for every $z \in \cS$, one can find a point $y \in \cY$ (possibly depending on $z$) satisfying $\bc(y, z) \leq -\zeta$.

issues.failure_explanation: The negation of the theorem only implies that for each $y$ there is some component $j$ (possibly depending on $y$) with $\bc_j(y,z^k)>-\zeta_k$. It does not imply the existence of a single $j$ that works for all $y\in\cY$. The proof's subsequent contradiction relies on this common $j$.

failure_location.quote:
Then there exist a positive sequence $\{\zeta_k\}$, a sequence $\{z^k\} \subset \cS$, and some $j \in \{1,...,m\}$ such that $\lim_{k\to\infty }\zeta_k = 0$ and  
\beq \label{bc-ineq1}
 \bc_{j}(y, z^k) > -\zeta_k \quad  \forall y\in\cY, \, \forall k.
\eeq

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the contradiction argument with a standard compactness argument: for each $z\in\cS$, MFCQ gives a direction making all active constraints strictly negative; by continuity and compactness of $\cS$, there is a uniform margin $\zeta>0$.
issues.overall_effect: The uniform Slater constant $\zeta$ is not established, so the uniform bound on Lagrange multipliers and all downstream convergence and complexity guarantees that use it are not rigorously supported.
issues.title: Invalid contradiction setup in uniform Slater proof
issues.why_classification: The theorem is true and the repair is standard, but it requires a nontrivial compactness argument and affects several downstream results.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof replaces $\|\hat y^k-z^k\|^2-\|z^{k+1}-z^k\|^2$ by $\|\hat y^k-z^{k+1}\|^2$, which is not valid in general (e.g., $z^k=0$, $\hat y^k=10$, $z^{k+1}=9$). It also omits $q$ from the definition of $\phi$, though the next line includes $q$. The final bound can be recovered by using the coarser valid bound $D_{\cY}^2$.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use the valid bound $\|\hat y^k-z^k\|^2-\|z^{k+1}-z^k\|^2 \le D_{\cY}^2$ and include $q$ in $\phi$; this yields the same bound $A$.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of the uniform multiplier bound is invalid as written, affecting the SCP convergence rate and downstream complexity results.
issues.title: False squared-norm inequality in Lagrange multiplier bound
issues.why_classification: The lemma statement is true and the repair is a short local correction that preserves the bound.

issues.failure_explanation: The termination inequality does not imply $\|z^{k+1}-z^k\| \le \tau/\omega$; the first term can be small even when the step is large. The conclusion $\dist(0,\partial\bh(z^{k+1},z^k))\le\tau$ follows directly from the termination inequality, so the theorem is true but the proof step is invalid.

failure_location.quote: By similar arugments as above, one has that $0<L_k \leq \bar{L}$, $\|\lambda^k\|_\infty \leq A$, and $\|z^{k+1}-z^k\| \leq  \tau/\omega$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the false inference with the direct observation that the termination condition itself bounds $\dist(0,\partial\bh(z^{k+1},z^k))$ by $\tau$.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of the SCP convergence rate contains an invalid inference, though the result can be repaired locally.
issues.title: False inference of step-size bound in SCP termination proof
issues.why_classification: The theorem remains valid and the repair is a short local argument.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: z^{k+1, i} = &\mathop{\arg\min}_z \Big\{ \langle \nabla g(z^k), z \rangle + \frac{L_{k, i}}{2}\|z - z^k\|^2 + q(z) \Big\} \\ &\qquad \text{s.t.} \quad \bc(z, z^k) \leq 0,
The functions $p, q$ are proper closed convex, and the proximal operators of $p$ and $q$ can be computed exactly.

issues.failure_explanation: The x- and z-updates are constrained proximal steps (with additional ball constraints), not the standard proximal operators of $p$ or $q$. The paper assumes only that the proximal operators of $p$ and $q$ can be computed exactly; it does not establish that these constrained subproblems can be solved with one such evaluation. Thus the prox evaluation counts in Theorem~\ref{thm:operations} are not justified.

failure_location.quote: x^{k+1} = \mathop{\arg\min}_{x \in \cB(x^k, r)} \Big\{ \langle \nabla_x f(x^{k}, y^{k}), x \rangle + \frac{\bar{L}_k}{2} \|x - x^k\|^2 + p(x) \Big\}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either specify how to solve the constrained subproblems using a bounded number of prox evaluations and include those in the count, or add an assumption that the constrained proximal operators can be computed exactly in one call.
issues.overall_effect: The proximal operator evaluation complexity in Theorem~\ref{thm:operations} is unsupported, although the gradient evaluation complexity may remain valid.
issues.title: Subproblems are not single proximal operator evaluations
issues.why_classification: It affects part of the advertised oracle complexity but not the main gradient complexity; a repair requires additional algorithmic specification.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
Suppose that $G_f < \infty$. Then it holds that
\beq \label{Af}
\|\lambda^{k,\ell}\|_1 \leq A_f:=\zeta^{-1}(G_f D_{\cY} + \bar{L}D_{\cY}^2/2 + M_q) \qquad \forall k, \ell.
\eeq

issues.failure_explanation: The bound $A_f$ and hence $\overline{K}_{f,\theta}$ and $\widehat{N}_\epsilon$ depend on $G_f$. If $G_f=\infty$, these constants are infinite and the stated finite complexity bound fails. Assumption~\ref{ass:Lip_Smo_KL} does not imply $G_f<\infty$ (e.g., $\cX$ can be unbounded and $f(x,y)=x^\top y$ satisfies the smoothness assumptions). The theorem omits the necessary hypothesis $G_f<\infty$.

failure_location.quote: Suppose that Assumptions \ref{ass:Lip_Smo_KL} and \ref{ass:MFCQ} hold. Then the total number of evaluations of the proximal operators of $p$ and $q$, and the gradient $\nabla f$ performed by Algorithm~\ref{algo_implement:whole} is at most $\widehat{K}_\epsilon$, $\widehat{N}_\epsilon$, and $\widehat{K}_\epsilon + \widehat{N}_\epsilon$, respectively, ...

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis $G_f<\infty$ (or that $\cX$ is compact) to Theorem~\ref{thm:operations} and to the problem setting.
issues.overall_effect: The first-order oracle complexity guarantee is not valid under the stated assumptions; it requires an additional boundedness condition on $\nabla_y f$ over $\cX\times\cY$ (or compactness of $\cX$).
issues.title: Missing bounded-gradient hypothesis in first-order oracle complexity theorem
issues.why_classification: It is a missing hypothesis that restricts the scope of the first-order oracle complexity result, though the main iteration complexity is unaffected.
